name: Greyson
why: Detroit golf-clothing house from 2015 — the Montauk performance trouser, printed polos, the wolf mark — with ten stores of its own and a Seoul store.
origin: Founded in 2015 in Hawthorne, New York (first HQ per Crain's Detroit 2019; HQ now Detroit, Michigan) by Charlie Schaefer.

craft_evidence.owned: NONE found (Our Story names no factory or workshop; HQ Detroit per press)
craft_evidence.makers: NONE for Greyson-made clothing (0 of 311 PDPs name a maker); collaboration partners Soft Goods (Detroit) and Del Toro (shoes) named in titles
craft_evidence.mills: NONE (18 of 311 pages say the fabric is Italian, mill unnamed; Fabric Library names no mill)
craft_evidence.madein: about 2% for garment country: "Made in USA"/"Crafted in Detroit" on the Soft Goods and Ford collaboration pieces, "Imported" on Serrano Dress Pant; 1 of 20 core PDPs sampled states anything; fabric origin (Italy) on 18 of 311
craft_evidence.heritage: dated in press only: founded 2015 by Charlie Schaefer after leaving Ralph Lauren; HQ Hawthorne, NY, then Detroit (Crain's Detroit 2019); site gives no date or place
craft_evidence.process: no (fabric-program descriptions only, no construction process)
craft_evidence.reasoning: No maker, mill or facility is named for Greyson-made clothing, and product pages almost never state where the garment is made. The Fabric Library and 18 product pages say the Montauk and Sequoia fabrics are Italian, unnamed; the only made-in-USA statements are on Soft Goods collaboration pieces made by a partner. Founding (2015) is dated only in press. 2 proposed for the checkable fabric-origin statements, 1 if those do not count.

ownership.owner: Private, founder-led (Charlie Schaefer, founder and CEO); $20M Series A Feb 2025 led by NewBound Ventures and Chris Koch (New Era CEO), with Tom Nolan and David Chu; no controlling owner disclosed
